summary.title: Small WLAN Threat Model
summary.description:
This threat model examines a small Wireless Local Area Network (WLAN) consisting of a wireless router or access point, a laptop, and a smartphone connected to the internet. The network allows users to access online services and share information wirelessly.

The assessment identifies important network assets, potential threats, vulnerabilities, and their possible impact on confidentiality, integrity, and availability. It also proposes security controls to reduce risks such as unauthorized access, eavesdropping, evil twin attacks, denial-of-service attacks, and malware infections.

diagrams.title: Small WLAN Network Architecture
diagrams.description: This threat model uses the STRIDE methodology to identify and assess security threats affecting a small Wireless Local Area Network (WLAN). STRIDE examines six threat categories: Spoofing, Tampering, Repudiation, Information Disclosure, Denial of Service, and Elevation of Privilege.  The assessment focuses on threats to the wireless router, connected devices, network communications, and user credentials. It evaluates how attackers could impersonate legitimate devices, modify transmitted data, deny users access to network services, expose sensitive information, or gain unauthorized privileges.  Appropriate security controls are proposed to protect the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of the WLAN.
